rationale.conceptual: Standard DFT method with careful implementation needed: selection of pseudopotentials, convergence tests, supercell relaxation, third-order Birch-Murnaghan EOS fitting, and Gibbs free energy derivation. Requires domain knowledge in solid-state physics and mineral physics but no novel algorithm.
rationale.execution: Pipeline has ~6 stages: DFT for pure references at multiple volumes, DFT for alloy supercell at multiple volumes, EOS fitting, volume expansion computation, static ΔG curve, entropy-corrected ΔG. Requires orchestrating multiple DFT jobs, managing data, and post-processing with custom scripts.

difficulty.reasoning: The task requires performing DFT calculations for a Fe-K alloy, fitting equations of state, and computing Gibbs free energy differences. The method is standard but non-trivial due to setup of DFT inputs, supercell construction, and EOS fitting. Execution involves multiple stages (DFT runs, fitting, post-processing) with tooling dependencies. Resource needs are moderate CPU-only, no GPU.

compute_estimate.reasoning: DFT plane-wave calculations for a 96-atom supercell with Fe and K are moderate CPU workloads (hundreds of hours on a single multi-core CPU) with memory needs around 32 GB RAM. No large datasets; pseudopotential files are tiny.
